symptom (what run 99's readback shows): job completes (consumer = producer, stamps advance), every output word still 0xdead0001, all fault registers 0
likely cause: no store reached memory: the lanes were disabled (thread-count dword not at common dword 2*nbuf, prologue W1 names another dword), or the store skip jumped (no lane active), or a store form that completes without storing (the A9 form)
registers / words to read next: binding PDS data and control words (dest dword = bits 13-20), the count block, prologue W1
how to tell the causes apart: put the count at the wrong dword on purpose: identical silence means this is the cause (run 98 was this case)

likely cause: one lane only: the thread-count dword still 0x00010001, or KERNEL8 workgroup_size_x - 1 = 0
how to tell the causes apart: value in out[0] is 0 either way; if out[0] = 0 and the count is right, check KERNEL8

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): out[i] = i only for i < 32 when N = 48/64/128
likely cause: the second 32-lane task never ran: workgroup_size_x - 1 below N - 1, or max_instances not 0
registers / words to read next: KERNEL8 (must be (hw_threads - 1) << 18, hw_threads = N rounded up to 32)
how to tell the causes apart: lid48: lanes 48-63 must stay sentinel (the prologue masks them)

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): values at the wrong places (out[2i] = i, out[i/2] = ...)
likely cause: wrong shift amount or a wrong half in the address build
registers / words to read next: the shift's W4 (0101 | n << 1); the addr instruction 3 W2 (B must be half 2*hi + 1)
how to tell the causes apart: carry1 isolates the carry half: wrong half = a fault at 0xffffffff_xxxxxxxx or a store elsewhere
tag: orchard-HW (iPod saw stores at 0x11_00100000 with the wrong half)

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): BIF fault, REQ_STATUS RNW = 0 (write), ADDRESS high bits non-zero (0x1_..., 0x11_..., 0xff_...)
likely cause: the high address word is wrong: the carry was not added, or the wrong half was
registers / words to read next: BIF_FAULT_BANK0_MMU_STATUS 0x12b0, REQ_STATUS 0x12b8 (+0x12bc high: ADDRESS is bits 39:4), BIF_FAULT_READ 0x13e0
how to tell the causes apart: the faulting ADDRESS minus the expected VA gives the error directly

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): job completes, loads give 0 (ldcopy4 out = 0) or the old register value
likely cause: the load did not read: a non-A8 load form (the A9/A10 2310 ... 8800 form stores nothing on the A8; its load is untested there), or the store read the register before the load landed (missing 004d)
registers / words to read next: the load words, the 004d after it
how to tell the causes apart: out = 0: the load executed but read nothing useful; out = the previous register content (e.g. the address low word): the wait is missing

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): BIF fault, RNW = 1 (read), ADDRESS = in VA + 4i
likely cause: the load address is wrong or the input page is not mapped in the job's context
registers / words to read next: same BIF registers; the argument table at heap+0x240
how to tell the causes apart: if ADDRESS = the expected VA the page is unmapped: map it (the heap is mapped, so inputs in the heap avoid this)

likely cause: every group read workgroup ID 0 (the IF1 DOUTW did not land in threadgroup word 0) or only one group ran (KERNEL3 = 0)
registers / words to read next: wgidraw4x32 (all 0 = the ID never arrives); KERNEL0 usc_common_size must be 1 (0x42106); kernel PDS data dword 2 = 0x90000002
how to tell the causes apart: wgidraw non-zero but gid wrong: the shift/add of the global index

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): gid with N = 4 wrong but N = 32 right
likely cause: several workgroups per task (max_instances 0 = 32 lanes = 8 groups of 4) mis-assigned: per-workgroup common store or IDs
registers / words to read next: KERNEL8 max_instances; try max_instances 4 (one group per task: 4 << 27) as the discriminator
how to tell the causes apart: if max_instances = 4 fixes it, keep one workgroup per task for small groups

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): no completion (consumer stays, stamps unchanged), no fault, watchdog reset at about 20 s
likely cause: the USC task never ends: end word not at a 64-byte boundary, a jump offset wrong (ISA.md: offsets >= 256 bytes need the bit-0 encoding), a loop that never breaks (count register beyond the allocation, a wrong compare), or a popped stack level a lane still waits on
first kernels where it can appear: loop5x4, loopdiv32, condodd32; also any kernel longer than its slot
registers / words to read next: read the stream and the kernel back from GPU memory before the job (a mis-placed kernel runs into the next item)
how to tell the causes apart: the loop kernels have a uniform variant first: uniform passes and divergent hangs = the stack/last-read rule

likely cause: the register is beyond the allocation: K0 usc_unified_size (bits 12-17, field 2n = 8n registers) and the DOUTU temps (PDS data dword 1, 0x10 per 8 registers) must both cover it; A10: no fault, wrong values
registers / words to read next: K0 and kernel PDS data dword 1
how to tell the causes apart: reg11a16 right and reg11a8 wrong = the allocation rule holds on J81

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): store to a read-only page (not in the library: set PTE bit 1 READ_ONLY on the output page and run lid4)
registers / words to read next: BIF_FAULT_BANK0_MMU_STATUS: FAULT (bit 0) and FAULT_RO (bit 4); REQ_STATUS RNW = 0, ADDRESS = 0x203000 >> 4 field
how to tell the causes apart: expect FAULT_RO set; if the job then never completes, the firmware does not recover from USC write faults (unknown on J81)

symptom (what run 99's readback shows): store one word beyond the mapped page (lid4 with the output VA at page end - 4, next page unmapped)
registers / words to read next: BIF bank 0 as above with FAULT set and FAULT_RO clear, ADDRESS = the next page; out[last-in-page] written
how to tell the causes apart: the in-page lanes' stores land before the fault (they are separate requests): a partial result plus one fault

likely cause: unknown: the memory unit may align the address down, split the access or fault
registers / words to read next: out[0], out[1] byte by byte; BIF registers
how to tell the causes apart: a value at out+0 = aligned down; bytes 2-5 = split; a fault = alignment checked. Test only after everything above passes
